verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai exēlthen ekeithen kai erchetai eis tēn patrida autou kai akolouthousin autō hoi mathētai autou
verses.literal: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown accompanied by His disciples
verses.literalPt: Tendo Jesus saído dali, foi para a sua terra, e seus discípulos acompanharam-no.

verses.original: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι
verses.transliteration: kai genomenou sabbatou ērxato didaskein en tē synagōgē kai hoi polloi akouontes exeplēssonto legontes Pothen toutō tauta kai tis hē sophia hē dotheisa toutō kai hai dynameis toiautai dia tōn cheirōn autou ginomenai
verses.literal: When the Sabbath came He began to teach in the synagogue and many who heard Him were astonished Where did this man get these ideas they asked What is this wisdom He has been given . . . And how can He perform . . . . . . . . . . . . such miracles
verses.literalPt: Chegando o sábado, começou a ensinar na sinagoga; e muitos, ao ouvi-lo, se admiravam, dizendo: Donde lhe vêm essas coisas e que sabedoria é esta que lhe é dada? Que significam tais milagres operados pela sua mão?

verses.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: ouch houtos estin ho tektōn ho huios tēs Marias kai adelphos Iakōbou kai Iōsētos kai Iouda kai Simōnos kai ouk eisin hai adelphai autou hōde pros hēmas kai eskandalizonto en autō
verses.literal: Isn’t . . . this the carpenter the son of Mary and the brother of James Joses Judas and Simon Aren’t . . . His sisters here with us as well And they took offense at Him
verses.literalPt: Não é este o carpinteiro, filho de Maria, irmão de Tiago, de José, de Judas e de Simão? E suas irmãs não estão aqui entre nós? Ele lhes servia de pedra de tropeço.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois ho Iēsous hoti Ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi autou kai en tois syngeneusin autou kai en tē oikia autou
verses.literal: Then Jesus said to them Only . . . in his hometown among his relatives and in his own household is a prophet without honor
verses.literalPt: Jesus lhes disse: Um profeta não deixa de receber honra senão na sua terra, entre os seus parentes e na sua casa.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν
verses.transliteration: kai ouk edynato ekei poiēsai oudemian dynamin ei mē oligois arrōstois epitheis tas cheiras etherapeusen
verses.literal: So He could not perform any miracles there except . . . to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them
verses.literalPt: Não podia fazer ali nenhum milagre, a não ser que pôs as mãos sobre alguns enfermos e os curou.

verses.original: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων
verses.transliteration: kai ethaumazen dia tēn apistian autōn Kai periēgen tas kōmas kyklō didaskōn
verses.literal: And He was amazed at their unbelief And He went around from village to village teaching the people
verses.literalPt: E admirou-se por causa da incredulidade do povo. Ele andava pelas aldeias circunvizinhas ensinando.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων
verses.transliteration: Kai proskaleitai tous dōdeka kai ērxato autous apostellein dyo dyo kai edidou autois exousian tōn pneumatōn tōn akathartōn
verses.literal: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out . . . two by two giving them authority over unclean spirits
verses.literalPt: Jesus chamou os doze, e começou a enviá-los dois a dois, e deu-lhes autoridade sobre os espíritos imundos;

verses.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον μὴ ἄρτον μὴ πήραν μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν
verses.transliteration: kai parēngeilen autois hina mēden airōsin eis hodon ei mē rhabdon monon mē arton mē pēran mē eis tēn zōnēn chalkon
verses.literal: He instructed them to take nothing but . . . . . . a staff for the journey no bread no bag no money in their belts
verses.literalPt: ordenou-lhes que nada levassem para o caminho, exceto bordão; nem pão, nem alforje, nem dinheiro na bolsa;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας
verses.transliteration: alla hypodedemenous sandalia kai mē endysēsthe dyo chitōnas
verses.literal: and to wear sandals but not a second tunic
verses.literalPt: mas que fossem calçados de sandálias e que não vestissem duas túnicas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Hopou ean eiselthēte eis oikian ekei menete heōs an exelthēte ekeithen
verses.literal: And He told them When . . . you enter . . . a house stay there until . . . you leave that area
verses.literalPt: Disse mais: Em qualquer casa onde entrardes, hospedai-vos aí até que vos retireis.

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai hos an topos mē dexētai hymas mēde akousōsin hymōn ekporeuomenoi ekeithen ektinaxate ton choun ton hypokatō tōn podōn hymōn eis martyrion autois
verses.literal: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place as a testimony against them
verses.literalPt: Se algum lugar não vos receber, nem os homens vos ouvirem, saindo dali, sacudi o pó dos vossos pés em testemunho contra eles.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthontes ekēryxan hina metanoōsin
verses.literal: So they set out and preached that the people should repent
verses.literalPt: Eles, saindo, pregaram ao povo que se arrependesse;

verses.original: καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον
verses.transliteration: kai daimonia polla exeballon kai ēleiphon elaiō pollous arrōstous kai etherapeuon
verses.literal: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick anointing them with oil
verses.literalPt: expeliam muitos demônios, ungiam com óleo a muitos enfermos e os curavam.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai ēkousen ho basileus Hērōdēs phaneron gar egeneto to onoma autou kai elegon hoti Iōannēs ho Baptizōn egēgertai ek nekrōn kai dia touto energousin hai dynameis en autō
verses.literal: Now King Herod heard about this for Jesus’ name had become well known and people were saying John the Baptist has risen from the dead That is why miraculous powers are at work in him
verses.literalPt: O rei Herodes soube disso (porque o nome de Jesus já se tornara conhecido), e alguns diziam: É João Batista que tem ressuscitado dentre os mortos; por isso, virtudes sobrenaturais nele operam.

verses.original: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν
verses.transliteration: alloi de elegon hoti Ēlias estin alloi de elegon hoti Prophētēs hōs heis tōn prophētōn
verses.literal: Others were saying He is Elijah and still others - He is a prophet like one of the prophets of old
verses.literalPt: Outros diziam: É Elias; outros ainda: É profeta como um dos profetas.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην οὗτος ἠγέρθη
verses.transliteration: Akousas de ho Hērōdēs elegen Hon egō apekephalisa Iōannēn houtos ēgerthē
verses.literal: But when Herod heard this he said John whom I beheaded has risen from the dead
verses.literalPt: Mas Herodes, ouvindo isso, dizia: É João, a quem eu mandei degolar e que ressurgiu.

verses.original: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν
verses.transliteration: Autos gar ho Hērōdēs aposteilas ekratēsen ton Iōannēn kai edēsen auton en phylakē dia Hērōdiada tēn gynaika Philippou tou adelphou autou hoti autēn egamēsen
verses.literal: For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound . . . and imprisoned on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias whom Herod had married
verses.literalPt: Pois o próprio Herodes mandara prender a João e acorrentá-lo no cárcere por causa de Herodias, mulher de seu irmão Filipe (Herodes se havia casado com ela);

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου
verses.transliteration: elegen gar ho Iōannēs tō Hērōdē hoti Ouk exestin soi echein tēn gynaika tou adelphou sou
verses.literal: For John had been telling Herod It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife
verses.literalPt: porque João lhe dizia: Não te é lícito ter a mulher de teu irmão.

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο
verses.transliteration: Hē de Hērōdias eneichen autō kai ēthelen auton apokteinai kai ouk ēdynato
verses.literal: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him But she had been unable
verses.literalPt: Herodias o odiava e queria matá-lo, mas não podia;

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν
verses.transliteration: ho gar Hērōdēs ephobeito ton Iōannēn eidōs auton andra dikaion kai hagion kai synetērei auton kai akousas autou polla ēporei kai hēdeōs autou ēkouen
verses.literal: because Herod feared John and protected him knowing that he was a righteous and holy man When he heard John’s words he was greatly perplexed yet he listened to him gladly
verses.literalPt: porque Herodes temia a João, sabendo que era homem reto e santo, e o retinha em segurança. Ao ouvi-lo, ficava muito perplexo e o escutava de boa vontade.

verses.original: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας
verses.transliteration: Kai genomenēs hēmeras eukairou hote Hērōdēs tois genesiois autou deipnon epoiēsen tois megistasin autou kai tois chiliarchois kai tois prōtois tēs Galilaias
verses.literal: On Herod’s birthday her opportunity . . . arose Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee
verses.literalPt: Oferecendo-se uma ocasião favorável, quando Herodes, no seu aniversário natalício, deu um banquete aos seus dignitários, aos oficiais militares e aos principais da Galileia,

verses.original: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τῷ κορασίῳ Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς καὶ δώσω σοι
verses.transliteration: kai eiselthousēs tēs thygatros autēs tēs Hērōdiados kai orchēsamenēs ēresen tō Hērōdē kai tois synanakeimenois ho de basileus eipen tō korasiō Aitēson me ho ean thelēs kai dōsō soi
verses.literal: When the daughter of Herodias - came and danced she pleased Herod and his guests and the king said to the girl Ask me for whatever you wish and I will give it to you
verses.literalPt: a filha da própria Herodias, tendo entrado, dançou e agradou a Herodes e aos seus convivas. O rei disse à moça: Pede-me o que quiseres, e eu to darei;

verses.original: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ Πολλά Ὅ¦τι ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου
verses.transliteration: kai ōmosen autē Polla HO¦ti ean me aitēsēs dōsō soi heōs hēmisous tēs basileias mou
verses.literal: And he swore to her Whatever you ask of me I will give you up to half my kingdom
verses.literalPt: e jurou-lhe: Se me pedires ainda mesmo a metade do meu reino, eu ta darei.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς Τί αἰτήσωμαι Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτίζοντος
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthousa eipen tē mētri autēs Ti aitēsōmai Hē de eipen Tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou Baptizontos
verses.literal: Then she went out and asked her mother What should I request And her mother answered The head of John the Baptist
verses.literalPt: Ela saiu e perguntou a sua mãe: Que pedirei? Esta respondeu: A cabeça de João Batista.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα Θέλω ἵνα ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai eiselthousa euthys meta spoudēs pros ton basilea ētēsato legousa Thelō hina exautēs dōs moi epi pinaki tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou Baptistou
verses.literal: At once the girl hurried back . . . . . . to the king with her request I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately
verses.literalPt: No mesmo instante, voltando apressadamente para o rei, disse: Quero que, sem demora, me dês num prato a cabeça de João Batista.

verses.original: Καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: Kai perilypos genomenos ho basileus dia tous horkous kai tous anakeimenous ouk ēthelēsen athetēsai autēn
verses.literal: The king was consumed with sorrow but because of his oaths and his guests he did not want to refuse her
verses.literalPt: O rei, embora muito triste, contudo, por causa do juramento e também dos convivas, não lha quis recusar.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ
verses.transliteration: kai euthys aposteilas ho basileus spekoulatora epetaxen enenkai tēn kephalēn autou kai apelthōn apekephalisen auton en tē phylakē
verses.literal: So without delay the king commanded that John’s head be brought in He sent an executioner who went and beheaded him in the prison
verses.literalPt: Imediatamente, o rei enviou um soldado da sua guarda com a ordem de trazer a cabeça de João. O soldado foi degolá-lo no cárcere,

verses.original: καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: kai ēnenken tēn kephalēn autou epi pinaki kai edōken autēn tō korasiō kai to korasion edōken autēn tē mētri autēs
verses.literal: The man brought . . . John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl - who gave it to her mother
verses.literalPt: trouxe a cabeça num prato e a deu à moça; e a moça a deu à sua mãe.

verses.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ
verses.transliteration: kai akousantes hoi mathētai autou ēlthon kai ēran to ptōma autou kai ethēkan auto en mnēmeiō
verses.literal: When John’s disciples heard about this they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb
verses.literalPt: Sabendo disso, vieram os seus discípulos, levaram-lhe o corpo e depositaram-no em um túmulo.

verses.original: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν
verses.transliteration: Kai synagontai hoi apostoloi pros ton Iēsoun kai apēngeilan autō panta hosa epoiēsan kai hosa edidaxan
verses.literal: Meanwhile the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news . . . of all . . . they had done and taught
verses.literalPt: Reunindo-se os apóstolos com Jesus, contaram-lhe tudo quanto haviam feito e ensinado.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν
verses.transliteration: kai legei autois Deute hymeis autoi kat’ idian eis erēmon topon kai anapausasthe oligon ēsan gar hoi erchomenoi kai hoi hypagontes polloi kai oude phagein eukairoun
verses.literal: And He said to them Come with Me privately . . . to a solitary place and let us rest for a while For many people were coming and going and they did not even have time to eat
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes disse: Vinde a um lugar solitário, à parte, e descansai um pouco. Pois eram muitos os que vinham e iam, e nem tinham tempo para comer.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν
verses.transliteration: Kai apēlthon en tō ploiō eis erēmon topon kat’ idian
verses.literal: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place
verses.literalPt: Então, foram sós na barca a um lugar deserto.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: kai eidon autous hypagontas kai epegnōsan polloi kai pezē apo pasōn tōn poleōn synedramon ekei kai proēlthon autous
verses.literal: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them
verses.literalPt: Muitos os viram partir e os reconheceram; correram para lá, a pé, de todas as cidades, e ali chegaram primeiro do que eles.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthōn eiden polyn ochlon kai esplanchnisthē ep’ autous hoti ēsan hōs probata mē echonta poimena kai ērxato didaskein autous polla
verses.literal: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd He had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd And He began to teach them many things
verses.literalPt: Ao desembarcar, viu Jesus uma grande multidão de homens e compadeceu-se deles, porque eram como ovelhas sem pastor; e começou a ensinar-lhes muitas coisas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή
verses.transliteration: Kai ēdē hōras pollēs genomenēs proselthontes autō hoi mathētai autou elegon hoti Erēmos estin ho topos kai ēdē hōra pollē
verses.literal: By now the hour was already late So the disciples came to Jesus and said - This is a desolate place and the hour is already late
verses.literalPt: Como a hora fosse já adiantada, chegaram-se a ele seus discípulos, dizendo: Este lugar é deserto, e já é muito tarde;

verses.original: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν
verses.transliteration: apolyson autous hina apelthontes eis tous kyklō agrous kai kōmas agorasōsin heautois ti phagōsin
verses.literal: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat
verses.literalPt: despede-os, para que vão aos sítios e às aldeias circunvizinhas comprar para si alguma comida.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν δηναρίων διακοσίων ἄρτους καὶ δώσομεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: Ho de apokritheis eipen autois Dote autois hymeis phagein Kai legousin autō Apelthontes agorasōmen dēnariōn diakosiōn artous kai dōsomen autois phagein
verses.literal: But Jesus told . . . them You give them something to eat They asked Him Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus disse: Dai-lhes vós de comer. Deveremos, disseram eles, ir comprar duzentos denários de pão e dar-lhes de comer?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους ὑπάγετε ἴδετε Καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν Πέντε καὶ δύο ἰχθύας
verses.transliteration: Ho de legei autois Posous echete artous hypagete idete Kai gnontes legousin Pente kai dyo ichthyas
verses.literal: Go and see how many loaves you have - He told them And after checking they said Five and two fish
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes perguntou: Quantos pães tendes? Ide ver. Depois de se terem informado, responderam: Cinco pães e dois peixes.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς ἀνακλῖναι πάντας συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai epetaxen autois anaklinai pantas symposia symposia epi tō chlōrō chortō
verses.literal: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass
verses.literalPt: Então, mandou aos discípulos que a todos fizessem sentar em grupos sobre a relva verde.

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ κατὰ πεντήκοντα
verses.transliteration: kai anepesan prasiai prasiai kata hekaton kai kata pentēkonta
verses.literal: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties
verses.literalPt: Sentaram-se em turmas de cem e de cinquenta.

verses.original: Καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai labōn tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas anablepsas eis ton ouranon eulogēsen kai kateklasen tous artous kai edidou tois mathētais autou hina paratithōsin autois kai tous dyo ichthyas emerisen pasin
verses.literal: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people And He divided the two fish among them all
verses.literalPt: Ele tomou os cinco pães e os dois peixes, e, erguendo os olhos ao céu, deu graças, e, partindo os pães, entregou-os aos discípulos para eles distribuírem; e repartiu por todos os dois peixes.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν
verses.transliteration: Kai ephagon pantes kai echortasthēsan
verses.literal: They all ate and were satisfied
verses.literalPt: Todos comeram e se fartaram;

verses.original: καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων
verses.transliteration: kai ēran klasmata dōdeka kophinōn plērōmata kai apo tōn ichthyōn
verses.literal: and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls . . . of broken pieces of bread and - fish
verses.literalPt: e recolheram doze cestos cheios de pedaços de pão e de peixe.

verses.original: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες
verses.transliteration: kai ēsan hoi phagontes tous artous pentakischilioi andres
verses.literal: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves
verses.literalPt: Os que comeram os pães foram cinco mil.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys ēnankasen tous mathētas autou embēnai eis to ploion kai proagein eis to peran pros Bēthsaidan heōs autos apolyei ton ochlon
verses.literal: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him . . . . . . . . . to Bethsaida while He dismissed the crowd
verses.literalPt: Em seguida, obrigou os seus discípulos a embarcar e passar adiante para o outro lado, a Betsaida, enquanto ele despedia a multidão.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι
verses.transliteration: kai apotaxamenos autois apēlthen eis to oros proseuxasthai
verses.literal: After bidding them farewell . . . He went up on the mountain to pray
verses.literalPt: Depois de se haver despedido do povo, foi ao monte para orar.

verses.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai opsias genomenēs ēn to ploion en mesō tēs thalassēs kai autos monos epi tēs gēs
verses.literal: When evening came the boat was in the middle of the sea and Jesus was alone on land
verses.literalPt: À tardinha, achava-se a barca no meio do mar, e ele, sozinho, em terra.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: kai idōn autous basanizomenous en tō elaunein ēn gar ho anemos enantios autois peri tetartēn phylakēn tēs nyktos erchetai pros autous peripatōn epi tēs thalassēs kai ēthelen parelthein autous
verses.literal: He could see that the disciples were straining to row because the wind was against them About the fourth watch of the night Jesus went out to them walking on the sea He intended to pass by them
verses.literalPt: Vendo-os embaraçados em remar (porque o vento lhes era contrário), pela quarta vigília da noite foi ter com eles, andando sobre o mar; e queria passar-lhes adiante.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀνέκραξαν
verses.transliteration: hoi de idontes auton epi tēs thalassēs peripatounta edoxan hoti phantasma estin kai anekraxan
verses.literal: but when they saw Him walking on the sea they cried out thinking He was a ghost
verses.literalPt: Porém eles, vendo-o andar sobre o mar, pensaram que era um fantasma e gritaram;

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν ὁ Δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Θαρσεῖτε ἐγώ εἰμι μὴ φοβεῖσθε
verses.transliteration: pantes gar auton eidon kai etarachthēsan ho De euthys elalēsen met’ autōn kai legei autois Tharseite egō eimi mē phobeisthe
verses.literal: for they all saw Him and were terrified But Jesus spoke up at once - - Take courage It is I Do not be afraid
verses.literalPt: porque todos o viram e se perturbaram. Mas, no mesmo instante, falando com eles, disse: Tende ânimo! Sou eu! Não temais!

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο
verses.transliteration: kai anebē pros autous eis to ploion kai ekopasen ho anemos kai lian ek perissou en heautois existanto
verses.literal: Then He climbed into the boat with them and the wind died down And the disciples were utterly . . . . . . astounded
verses.literalPt: Entrou na barca para ir ter com eles, e cessou o vento. Eles se encheram de grande pasmo,

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη
verses.transliteration: ou gar synēkan epi tois artois all’ ēn autōn hē kardia pepōrōmenē
verses.literal: for they had not understood about the loaves but their hearts had been hardened
verses.literalPt: porque não haviam compreendido o milagre dos pães; ao contrário, o seu coração estava endurecido.

verses.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν
verses.transliteration: Kai diaperasantes epi tēn gēn ēlthon eis Gennēsaret kai prosōrmisthēsan
verses.literal: When they had crossed over they landed . . . . . . . . . at Gennesaret and moored the boat
verses.literalPt: Depois de feita a travessia, chegaram à terra de Genesaré e ali atracaram.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: kai exelthontōn autōn ek tou ploiou euthys epignontes auton
verses.literal: As soon as they got out of the boat the people recognized Jesus
verses.literalPt: Quando desembarcaram, o povo logo reconheceu a Jesus e,

verses.original: περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: periedramon holēn tēn chōran ekeinēn kai ērxanto epi tois krabattois tous kakōs echontas peripherein hopou ēkouon hoti estin
verses.literal: and ran through that whole region carrying the sick . . . on mats to wherever they heard He was
verses.literalPt: correndo por toda aquela região, começaram a trazer nos leitos os que se achavam doentes, para onde ouviam dizer que ele estava.

verses.original: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο
verses.transliteration: kai hopou an eiseporeueto eis kōmas ē eis poleis ē eis agrous en tais agorais etithesan tous asthenountas kai parekaloun auton hina kan tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou hapsōntai kai hosoi an hēpsanto autou esōzonto
verses.literal: And wherever . . . He went . . . villages and towns and countrysides they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak And all who touched Him were healed
verses.literalPt: Onde quer que ele entrava, fosse nas aldeias, ou nas cidades, ou nos campos, punham os doentes nas praças e lhe rogavam que os deixasse tocar ao menos na fímbria da sua capa; e todos os que nela tocaram ficavam sãos.
